NPA: The next chapter

By: Johann Botha | Production

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
After a lot of bad press NPA head Shawn Abrahams seemed to regain some credibility this week. But is it enough to save his job?

Unique Selling Point:
In-depth analysis of how this weeks' revelations about the letters between Shawn Abrahams froTm the NPA and Berning Ntlemeza from the Hawks, changes the turbulent political landscape

Summary:
To avoid being taken to court by the HSF and FuL ngo's, President Zuma this week asked the head of the NPA and two of his directors to supply reasons before 28/11 as to why he should not suspend them while the outcome of the enquiry into the Ghordan debacle is pending. In the almost 300 page affidavit Abrahams then submitted in return were letters between himself and the head of the Hawks Berning Ntlemeza. This exchange between the two heads seems to show that the Hawks did not want to back down on prosecuting Ghordan, and that they may have been trying to prescribe to the NPA how to act. From the letters it seems that Abrahams did not bend under the pressure. But what does it all mean? Is the president simply playing for time by sending out these letters, and is this enough proof that Abrahams acted independently throughout the Ghordan case? To date no head of the NPA since 1994 has managed to complete his contract term. We speak to various analysts to find out why.

Flight from Bloemfontein to Jhb for Carmel Rickard

Press Release:


After much bad press, the so called ‘captured’ NPA head, advocate Shaun Abrahams has seemed to regain credibility in recent days. But is it enough to save his job? An exchange of heated letters between Abrahams and head of the Hawks Berning Ntlemeza has revealed just how unhappy Ntlemeza was about the NPA’s decision to set aside fraud charges against Pravin Gordhan. Carte Blanche asks: just another twist in an ongoing saga, or could Abrahams follow the same route as his predecessors?

Script:


V/o On Monday President Jacob Zuma sent a letter to the head of the National Prosecuting Authority or NPA, Advocate Shaun Abrahams, to ask for reasons why he should not be suspended pending an enquiry into his fitness to hold office.
Devi Link Some say being appointed head of the NPA is like being handed a poisoned chalise. Since 1998, not a single one has seen out his term
V/o "The head of the NPA is appointed for a 10 year term - Abrahams has only been in the hot seat for 18months.
Theoretically we should only be on the second term at the moment – yet we are already on National Director of the NPA number 7.
Journalist Mandy Wiener says it's all about having someone there that you can control "
Mandy When they become too independent, when they are not sufficiently maleable, they are moved aside
V/o Prof Dirk Kotze agrees
Prof Kotze This is where the NPA is exceptionally attractive for the president and other senior persons because they can use this to either create suspicion about a person by saying you are being investigated by the hawks and ultimately by the NPA or, to be charged. And ultimately those persons are then excluded or eliminated from the political process or the political situation and that is what makes the national Director so absolutely fatally attractive for any poltician
V/o One common denominator throughout has been the decision on whether or not to prosecute President Zuma on the now infamous 783 charges against him.
Mandy Wiener Because ultimately, if you look at Zuma's end game, and no one knows what Zuma's endgame really is – he needs to be sure that he isn't prosecuted for corruption when he leaves office in a few years time. And the person who is going to decide whether or not he is prosecuted is the national Direactor of Public Prosecutions.
V/o When Adv Shaun Abrahams was appointed last year, the reputation of the NPA was in tatters. But he insisted that he was truly independent and that he was not scared to prosecute anyone
Shaun Abrahams I can assure you that I dont intend to use my powers to protect anybody. Does that answer your question. And i've not been appointed to protect anybody.
V/o "Yet many experts suspected him of being a Zuma man. As they did of the head of the hawks, Berning Ntlemeza. The fear was that the two of them would make a formidable team, against whom no opponent of pres Zuma would stand a chance.
Another fatal attraction for a political leader would be control of treasury. "
Prof Kotze And that I think is what we want to avoid – that these institutions of the state are actually abused or misused by important politicians. I would call that the real state capture.
V/o In December last year pres Zuma unexpectedly fired respected minister of finance Nhlanhla Nene, and appointed unknown Des van Rooyen in his place. The economy almost collapsed because of what was seen as an openly political move, and the president was forced to recall van Rooyen after only 3 days in office and bring back a Mbeki man, Pravin Ghordan in the hope that his credibility would save the Rand. But it became increasingly clear that there was tension between the president and Pravin Ghordan. Piet Olivier from the Helen Suzman Foundation says everyone was watching this closely
Helen Suzman Fndtn There are many reports that the minister stands in the way of a certain faction within the ruling party, that wants to use the treasury for their own personal enrichment, but again this is not something that we can pronounce on with certainty
V/o V/o
Shaun Abrahams On the recommendation of the prosecutor and having perused the evidence and in consultation with the director of public prosecution for Gauteng, Msenyathi, the acting special director of public prosecutions and head of the priority crimes litigation unit, dr Torie Pretorius, SC, has decided that mr Pillay, mr Magashula and mr Ghordan must be prosecuted.
V/o It was obvious to everyone except Abrahams apparently, that none of the four charges brought against the three accused stood any chance of success in a court.
HSF On any plausible reading of the facts, there is no way these charges could ever be proven, so at best this was breathtaking incompetence on the part of the NPA
V/o Legal writer and author Carmel Rickard agrees
Carmel If you have a look at how the the prosecution was announced and then the charges were announced as being withdrawn, the incompetence that was shown there was really quite gobsmacking really.
V/o In what was seen as a follow-up move to the announcement Zuma supporters within the ANC such immediately started calling for Ghordan's suspension or resignation. The public reaction, including many very senior ANC members was so immense that Ghordan became virtually untouchable and managed for the second time to deliver his budget speech. 5 days later Abrahams dropped the charges.
Abrahams In the circumstances I decided to overrule the decision to prosecute mr Magashula, mr Pillay and minister `ghordan on the charges listed on the summonses.
V/o Abrahams refused to resign over this and claimed that this was somehow proof of his independence, but the world interpreted it as the exact opposite. The very next day, two civic geoups, Freedom under law and the Helen Suzman Foundation wrote a letter to the president, asking him to suspend Abrahams
HSF The president claimed not to have received our letter, which we found puzzling because we sent it to various email adresses many of which were on the presidents website as email adresses to reach him. They were also on the national government directory, and also the president admitted that one of the email adresses was correct. But regardless, the president didn't need a letter from us to know that he was obliged and that it was prudent for him to suspend mr Abrahams. Because he kbew all about the charges, he knew they were bogus from the start and he knew they were eventually dropped.
V/o The two civic groups then filed an application for an urgent interdict from the court . When Abrahams, who was second respondent, filed his papers this week, it contained a letter, dated the 14th, from the president asking for reasons why he shouldn't be suspended. This move seemed to catch everyone by surprise. Some analysts predicted there was no case anymore as the president now did act, and that at the same time he has paved the way to drag the case out for months or longer. Legal writer Carmel Rickard disagrees
Carmel Rickard I think when he wrote this he was trying to make sure that the courts couldnt say that he hadnt applied his mind. But the wording of it comes out as an admission of something else. Namely that he only applied his mind because he was provoked into doing so by the intervention of these organisations
V/o Two days later, on thursday the presidents papers indeed claimed that the application was not urgent, and asked that the court dismiss the application with costs. However, by Friday, the organisations made it clear that they are not withdrawing the application
HSF Everyday that mr Abrahams is in the NPA is one that dengrates and reduces the credibility of the NPA.The president should take decisive action and the time he is taking now is not decisive
V/o Abrahams' papers also contained another surprise – an email excahnge between him and head of the hawks, Berning Ntlemeza which started the day before his announcement to withdraw the charges against Ghordan
Mandy At the heart of it you can see how angry they are and how Berning Ntlemezareally has a go sayin Shaun Abrahams acted in bad faith and that he gave in to the noise being created by the politicians and by the media and Abrahams kicks back saying well I take umbrage with you saying that I acted in bad fait. And I think that what Abrahams has done here is that he's released this correspndence in an attempt to show that he is not doing the bidding of Ntlemeza. And I think that he is being quite strategic about this. But I think here he has really played his trump card.
Devi link Nobody knowa how this will play out or when it will end, but this isnt just about president jacob Zuma and Shaun Abrahams – this is about our constitution.
Carmel That constitution that we put together at the time of transition in SA is a gift to the people of SA, it's a gift to us that we should respect and enjoy and savour and value. And its really difficult to understand how it is that we've got to the point of not feeling as passionate about it as we ought...

Promo 10 secs President Zuma this week asked Shaun Abrahams to supply reasons why he shouldn't be suspended as Director of the NPA. But Civic Rights groups are still taking the matter to court. What does it all mean?

Promo 15secs "V/o: Will Shaun Abrahams remain as Director of the NPA after the Ghordan debacle?
HSF: On any plausible reading of the facts, there is no way these charges could ever be proven, so at best this was breathtaking incompetence on the part of the NPA
V/o: What will the president do, and what will the court say?"
Promo 15secs "Acrimonius emails between the Hawks and the NPA surfaced this week
Soundup: Mandy
Who is on whose side in the fight over control of our law enforcement agencies?"
